daySheets.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: six-pose full-body expression model sheet for the original heyNag moth.
Input image1 is the ABSOLUTE CHARACTER IDENTITY and day palette master. Draw the SAME tiny, innocent moth six times in different emotions. Preserve the existing contemporary clean 2D comic look, gentle shading and bold soft charcoal outlines.
Layout: EXACTLY 3 columns by 2 rows in a 1536x1024 landscape transparent canvas; six equal square cells of512x512. Row-major order specified below. One complete full-body character centered in each cell at the SAME scale. Each character and any small cue must fit within its cell with comfortable margins. Keep baseline consistent except where specifically described. No cell borders, labels, numbers, text or background.
NONNEGOTIABLE IDENTITY: head remains HUGE and softly fluffy, about twice tiny torso width; almost no neck, tiny rounded cream body. Exactly TWO tiny mitten hands with one thumb hint, exactly TWO stubby green feet immediately beneath torso; no visible long shins, elongated forearms, waist, shoulder swagger, adult stance or large fingers. Both antennae keep their rounded paddle tips: VIEWER-RIGHT always longer, viewer-left shorter, even when flexed. Keep FOUR wing panels visible: pale green broad forewings overlapping smaller richer green hindwings, one subdued green teardrop per forewing, rounded distinct tips; no cape, cloth, sharp wings or extra wings.
Change facial emotion, small head angle, compact hands, slight wing opening and antenna bends ONLY. Preserve face fullness, eye spacing, overall head/body scale and lineweight. No nose, teeth, eyelashes, blush, muscular outlines, hats, costumes or scenery. The master should remain recognizable even in difficult emotions. Use warm cream, charcoal, pale celadon and chartreuse exactly as the reference. Mouth interior green when open. Hands may meet chin by lowering the head slightly, NEVER by growing arms.
No mature smirks, slanted predatory eyes, long limbs, raised adult hips, romantic human styling, material realism, paper texture, cast shadows, halos, furniture or scene. All space outside the six characters and permitted tiny cues is genuine alpha transparency.

Exact row-major expressions, top row left-to-right then bottom row left-to-right:
1. Curious: big attentive oval eyes look slightly to viewer-right; eyebrows softly raised, small questioning smile. Head inclines toward an imagined detail, tiny mittens pause near the belly; long antenna reaches first and short antenna trails. Feet planted, no question-mark icon.
2. Thinking with glasses: softly rectangular charcoal frames with CLEAR lenses and eyes visible looking upward. One tiny mitten touches the underside of the lower chin; the other tiny mitten supports that short elbow across the upper belly. Tip the big head DOWN a little to meet the hand, rather than lengthening an arm. Close elbows, softly pursed small mouth, relaxed long antenna curved in thought; one stub foot has a tiny toe pivot but stays beneath the body. Thoughtful and adorable, not stern professor.
3. Happy: small open green smile and two warm open oval eyes, relaxed tiny hands open close beside the belly. Both stub feet grounded, softly lifted antenna tips, wings resting open. Easy contented happiness; no giant leap.
4. Mischievous: one eye peacefully closed and the other SOFTLY half-open as if pretending to nap and peeking to see whether someone noticed; small rounded central U smile, gentle single brow lift. Head turns only a little; one tiny mitten near mouth, the other tucked beside belly. Long antenna innocently upright while short tip folds slightly. A sweet cheeky secret, never a mature sarcastic smirk, pointy eyes or hips.
5. Aha: bright open eyes, small delighted open green mouth, tiny hands lift just beside the ruff. Head and long antenna lift a little, wings open slightly without growing. ONE tiny warm light bulb sits clear of the tall antenna with two short light ticks; no other props.
6. Oops: lifted inner brow and small wobbly apologetic smile, a short head dip, one little mitten touches the side of the fluffy head and the other opens near the belly. Antenna tips droop unevenly; feet planted. Harmless clumsy surprise with a friendly recovery, no sweat drop or extra symbols.
Keep all SIX characters equally tiny and innocent. Same model, different emotional acting. No captions.

Exact row-major expressions, top row left-to-right then bottom row left-to-right:
1. Laughing: eyes close into joyful arcs, small wide green laughing mouth, cheeks keep original shape. One tiny mitten covers lower mouth, other rests on belly, body gives a very small forward chuckle bend. Antenna tips bounce in opposing soft curves; feet grounded.
2. Excited: wide bright oval eyes and delighted open green mouth; both tiny mittens raised beside lower cheeks without long arms. Tiny buoyant hop with feet just below body, wings open wider while preserving4panels. Two short low motion ticks allowed, no stars.
3. Proud: eyes gently closed, small satisfied U smile, head lifted a little, BOTH tiny mittens rest together on upper belly. A modest little pleased glow of posture with body unchanged and feet grounded. Antennae lift calmly, not triumph, swagger, hands-on-hips or adult chest.
4. Grateful: warm attentive eyes, gentle closed smile and small head bow toward viewer. Both tiny mittens meet over upper chest below ruff, elbows stay short. Wings soften downward, long antenna bends toward visitor. No text or symbols.
5. Affectionate: soft happy crescent eyes, small warm smile, little mittens together just in front of belly as if offering kindness. ONE small green heart floats close above hands, not covering body or ruff. Head gently tilted, antennae curve inward while keeping unequal lengths. No kissing lips or human romantic pose.
6. Shy: open oval eyes glance gently sideways/down, small tucked smile, head lowers modestly; tiny mittens meet at low belly, feet turn slightly inward directly below torso. Antennae tuck closer without crossing. No shrinking head, stretched neck, blush or teen posing.
Keep all SIX characters equally tiny and innocent. Same model, different emotional acting. No captions.

Exact row-major expressions, top row left-to-right then bottom row left-to-right:
1. Confused: one rounded brow up, other mildly pinched, small sideways uncertain mouth. Head tips back slightly from the imagined puzzle; both tiny mittens open near belly in a compact questioning gesture. Antennae point in different soft directions; clear difference from curious forward lean. No question mark.
2. Focused with glasses: same clear rounded-rectangle charcoal frames as thinking. Both oval eyes OPEN and attentive, brows softly lowered without angry V, mouth a tiny concentrated line. Head inclines forward; two tiny mittens rest close together in front of belly as if preparing a careful task, no chin-support pose. Long antenna aims steadily ahead, wings quietly tucked; no desk or device.
3. Skeptical: one soft eyebrow lifts, one eyelid sits just a little lower, SMALL central straight mouth rather than grin; eyes look slightly sideways. Both mittens remain close across belly without broad human crossed forearms. Tiny head tilt away, long antenna gently hooks back. Innocent 'really?' reaction, not adult cynicism.
4. Surprised: both eyes tall and fully open, brows high, small circular green O mouth. Tiny mittens hover just clear of lower cheeks, antennae lift almost straight but remain rounded and unequal. Short feet planted close, four wings slightly lifted. No symbol.
5. Relieved: eyes softly shut, tiny relaxed smile with a small breathing-out mouth, head and shoulders drop a fraction while body remains plump. One mitten over upper chest, other hangs loosely by belly. Antennae relax outward, wings settle. ONE small curved breath stroke beside mouth, not smoke or text.
6. Sleepy: heavy rounded half-lids and tiny soft yawn, one mitten rubs lower cheek near an eye while other rests against belly. Head nods toward shoulder with no added neck, antennae droop softly, feet grounded. No bed, moon, pillow, nightcap, or Z letters; same daylight palette.

1. Sad: inner brows gently lifted, open oval eyes lowered, very small downturned mouth. Head bows; tiny mittens hang close to sides, antennae lower and wings settle close. ONE small clear tear on one cheek, no waterfalls. Preserve round face and plump little body.
2. Worried: raised inner brows, attentive oval eyes looking forward, small uncertain wavy mouth. Tiny mittens clasp just below ruff, body stays upright and small. Long antenna arcs into a worried question-like CURVE but no actual symbol; short one lowers. No tear; visually distinct from sad and scared.
3. Scared: wide oval eyes and raised brows, small open green O mouth; tiny mittens pull close against lower cheeks as if bracing. Head tucks slightly into ruff, wings draw in and antennae lean back. Both stub feet remain under round body. A tiny startled vulnerable creature, no elongated scream face.
4. Frustrated: brows mildly knit, BOTH eyes squeezed shut, small strained wavy pout. BOTH tiny mittens huddle immediately below ruff; big head dips toward them without stretching arms. Long antenna bends into a soft defeated arch while short one dips. One stub toe poised to tap in place under body; frustration with a puzzle, not fury. No vein symbol.

Create the night counterpart of image1 by changing ONLY color and edge-lighting. Preserve EXACTLY the same six poses, facial expressions, eye and mouth shapes, hand locations, head/body ratio, tiny stub feet, all antenna positions, four layered wings, wing markings, glasses if present, props/cues, cell order, framing and pixels of alpha silhouette. Do not redraw expressions, add details or change anatomy.
Use image2's subtly warmer custard cream on face/body, softly warmer muted green forewings and recognizable chartreuse. Add only image2's fine restrained muted warm-olive outer edge light so antenna stems and contours separate from #1C1C1C. Inner outlines and eyes stay charcoal. Keep clean matte comic shading, no white sticker border or fuzzy surrounding glow. Preserve clear lenses, if present, with cream face visible and solid oval dark eyes.
